cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster. No warm-up, no small talk. David's very first words are "Help, O LORD," and then he tells the LORD what's wrong.

cards.question: David cries out to the LORD for help. What does he say has gone missing?

cards.text: And the people who are still around? David says they lie to one another, with flattering lips and a double heart.

cards.question: David says the liars around him speak with flattering lips and a double heart. What's a double heart?

answers.text: Saying one thing and meaning another
Being brave one day and scared the next
Loving two friends at the same time

cards.text: It's a gorgeous cookie box with a big shiny bow on top, and you open it up and it's EMPTY. Next, David has a word about mouths like that.

cards.question: David says, may the LORD cut off every flattering lip and every boastful tongue.

cards.text: Now David lets us hear the smooth talkers for ourselves. And friend... they are CONFIDENT.

cards.question: The smooth talkers in David's psalm brag about how they're going to win. What do they say they'll win with?
The smooth talkers in David's psalm say they answer to the LORD.

cards.text: "We own our lips—who can be our master?" I said "NOBODY tells me what to do" one time. Then the oven timer went off, and friend, I RAN.
Then the psalm takes a turn. Somebody new has something to say.

cards.question: Right in the middle of David's psalm, a new voice speaks up. Whose voice is it?
The LORD says He will now arise for the cause of the ___ and for the groaning of the needy.

cards.text: The LORD promises, "I will bring safety to him who yearns." And after all that lying and bragging, David turns to talk about the LORD's words.

cards.question: The liars' words were flattering and double-hearted. What does David say the words of the LORD are?

cards.text: David says they're like silver refined in a furnace, like gold purified sevenfold. SEVEN times through the fire, and I can't get ONE batch through the oven without forgetting the timer.

cards.question: David compares the LORD's words to silver refined in a furnace and gold purified seven times. What's that picture saying about the LORD's words?

answers.text: They cost a lot to get

cards.question: David talks straight to the LORD. He says the LORD will keep them and guard them ___ from this generation.
In the last line of his psalm, David says the wicked have all been driven away.

cards.text: David ends his psalm right there: "The wicked wander freely, and vileness is exalted among men."

findings.problem: The card cites Psalm 12:2-3, but it doesn't tell anything from verse 3. The joke is about verse 2, and "David has a word about mouths like that" only sets up the next card without telling what verse 3 says. The citation should be Psalm 12:2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke opens with "It's a gorgeous cookie box" without saying what "it" is. The baker has to work out that it means flattering lips or a double heart. The image also doesn't fully fit: a double heart means one thing outside and another inside, not nothing inside. The comparison should name what it's describing and match the core action of saying one thing and meaning another.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The card opens with the quote "We own our lips—who can be our master?" and never says who is speaking. The speaker should be named before the quote, for example "The smooth talkers say..."

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD will keep "them" and guard "them," but nothing on screen says who "them" is. The text also says "us" (Psalm 12:7), which includes David, so "them" changes who is being kept and guarded. The question should use "us" or say who is meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. Of the 11 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice, 3 are true or false and 2 are fill in the blank. That's double the true or false cards and triple the fill in the blank cards.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
